sectors.name: Technology
themes: Indonesia's accelerating fixed-wireless and fiber broadband penetration underpins durable revenue growth for INET and WIFI, insulated from global rate cycles.
Local-currency digital payment and e-commerce enablers (YELO, CENT) benefit from rising domestic consumption and government push for financial inclusion, a multi-year structural tailwind.
US-listed tech weakness is driving capital rotation into ASEAN-listed tech, favoring names with domestic earnings and lower dollar debt exposure.
sectors.ai: Buy pullbacks in Indonesia-listed tech names tied to domestic digital infrastructure (INET, WIFI) and local-currency revenue, as the ID outperformance vs US signals rotation into EM tech. Avoid US-exposed laggards; trim on any rally in VTNY/IRSX. Accumulate YELO on strength, CENT on dips.

Banking names (BDMN, 2881) are supported by stable NIMs and improving loan growth, but upside hinges on macro rate trajectory and credit quality, making them lower-beta core holdings.
sectors.ai: Buy pullbacks in AHAP, RELI, and BDMN on strong retail-driven momentum, but keep exposure barbelled with ERIE and AMAR for insurance upside. Sector breadth is neutral, so avoid chasing INDO and 2881 after sharp moves; add on 2-3% dips. US financials' mild strength supports sentiment, yet local catalysts remain stock-specific. Trim any laggards to recycle into leaders.

sectors.name: Mining & Energy
themes: Indonesian thermal coal export prices remain structurally supported by Asian demand and domestic market obligations, sustaining margin expansion for low-cost producers like BYAN and COAL.
Coal logistics and infrastructure names (ALKA, PSAB) are re-rating as port and haulage bottlenecks persist, creating durable pricing power and volume growth.
US LNG and gas infrastructure exposure (TRGP, BAJA) provides a hedge against Indonesian regulatory risk while capturing North American energy demand growth.
sectors.ai: Buy selective thermal coal and coal-midstream names (BYAN, ALKA, COAL) into strength; the +19.97% BYAN move signals tight domestic supply and high export pricing. Rotate out of laggards (INDY, MYOH) into high-beta coal logistics and contractors with order-book catalysts. Hold TRGP/BAJA for US LNG-linked upside. Watch for profit-taking after the 1.86% ID surge, but maintain longs on structural Indonesian coal demand through 2025.

sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
themes: Indonesia's 2025-2035 RUPTL expansion and mandatory carbon exchange are structurally boosting local EPC and IPP margins, favoring BATR and POWR regardless of global rate swings.
US utility outperformance is now driven by AI-driven load growth and grid hardening, not macro beta, making EIX, PCG, and SRE resilient but range-bound without Fed cuts.
Climate-tech supply chains face bifurcation: US solar (FSLR) benefits from IRA reshoring, while Indonesian nickel-linked storage names remain hostage to China's export quotas and EV demand.
sectors.ai: Buy selective Indonesia-exposed renewables names (BATR, POWR) on the government's accelerated RUPTL and carbon trading momentum, but stay defensive on US utilities (EIX, PCG) where rate-cut delays cap upside. Rotate into solar equipment (FSLR) only on tariff clarity; avoid laggards until volume confirms.

sectors.ai: Buy selective small-cap consumer names showing volume-driven re-rating (PADA, JARR, PGUN) as domestic demand stabilizes, but avoid chasing BEEF/AGAR momentum without earnings confirmation. Rotate into defensive staples with dividend support (SMGA, SIPD) for carry, and trim any exposure to US-linked names given the +0.20% lag. Position for Q3 festive seasonality by accumulating mid-cap FMCG with strong rural distribution now.

sectors.name: Infrastructure
themes: Indonesia's accelerated national strategic project (PSN) pipeline, including toll roads and ports, is a durable demand driver for contractors like KIJA and YPAS through 2025-2026.
Telecom tower and data-center infrastructure (TOWR, PACK) benefits from structural digital adoption and 5G rollout, with recurring lease revenue insulating against construction cyclicality.
Domestic infrastructure outperformance vs US (-1.28%) reflects local monetary easing expectations and fiscal stimulus, favoring IDX-listed operators over global-linked peers in a rate-cut cycle.
sectors.ai: Buy selective Indonesian infrastructure names with confirmed order books (KIJA, TOWR) and avoid chasing speculative penny movers (ASLI, TEBE) lacking earnings support. The sector's aggregate gain masks divergence—domestic strength (+1.73%) vs US drag (-1.28%) favors local toll, tower, and data-center plays. Accumulate on dips toward 0.39% aggregate, targeting KIJA and TOWR for 3-6 month upside as government capex accelerates ahead of 2025 elections.

sectors.name: Healthcare
themes: Indonesia's hospital operators (RSGK, LABS) are consolidating mid-tier facilities, driving durable same-store revenue growth as private insurance penetration rises.
Global plasma-derived therapies (CSL) face a multi-year supply-demand gap, underpinning pricing power and margin expansion beyond cyclical recovery.
Obesity and metabolic drug pipelines (LLY, PODD) are shifting care delivery toward chronic disease management, creating durable demand for delivery devices and companion diagnostics.
sectors.ai: Healthcare's aggregate uptick is broad-based, not idiosyncratic, with global large-caps (LLY, ABBV, JNJ) and Indonesia's RSGK/LABS confirming a risk-on rotation into defensive growth. Buy pullbacks in CSL (plasma pricing power) and RSGK (domestic hospital consolidation), but trim PODD after its 5.96% pop—valuation is stretched. Position for sustained M&A and GLP-1 spillover into diagnostics and distribution.

sectors.name: Logistics

Government infrastructure spending on toll roads and ports reduces transit costs and improves asset utilization, a multi-year margin tailwind for listed logistics firms, particularly KJEN and MITI.
sectors.ai: Buy logistics selectively on domestic volume recovery and port efficiency gains; KJEN, PORT, and SOCI lead with earnings momentum while TMAS offers scale. US weakness is a headwind for global names, so overweight ID-centric operators. Add RMKE for coal haulage tailwind; trim TAXI on speculative froth. Position for Q3 volume data and tariff-driven rerating.

US-linked entertainment names remain sensitive to global rate and ad-spend cycles, making them more volatile and less reliable for long-term compounding compared to domestic peers.

Rotate into TGUK and FORU for value catch-up; hold overall sector exposure at neutral with tight stops, as WATCH signal implies consolidation risk near-term.

sectors.name: Crypto & Digital Assets
themes: Indonesian retail crypto adoption is accelerating via local exchange tokens (BTW, VVV), creating a durable, high-volatility alpha pool decoupled from global majors.
Regulatory clarity under Bappebti is maturing, lowering delisting risk and attracting institutional custody flows into compliant local digital-asset listings.
Meme-coin and pump-token cycles (PUMP, SKY) are recurring structural drivers, with social-media-driven liquidity spikes offering outsized but short-lived returns.
sectors.ai: Rotate into high-beta Indonesian crypto proxies (BTW, VVV, PUMP) as global digital-asset sentiment stabilizes; the +16.7% BTW surge signals local retail conviction returning. Fade laggards like MATIC/POL until Ethereum-layer narratives revive. Position tactically for 2-4 week momentum, but trim into any BTC pullback below $60k—the sector remains sentiment-driven, not fundamentally repriced.
